about: Task hints: a hint for 18 tasks, none for the Open-dimension tasks, a layer separate from the task notes in agp_core/task_notes.json (which hold only the official scoring requirements). The hints reach the agent only with the opt-in switch OURS_TASK_HINTS (agp_core/features.py; on in the fixed system, SYSTEM there): agp_core/run_agent.py then appends the hint of the episode's official task, verbatim under the heading "# Hints for this task", right after the notes section (agp_core/task_notes.py hint_section, launch_hint_section; launch.json task_hint). One entry per base task in `hints` (the official task name without _random); a _random configuration uses its base task's hint; a task without an entry gets no section. agp_core/task_notes.py reads `hints` only.

hints.build_tower: Prefer to set up a pair of pillars together first, and then put the board on top of them. When picking up a wooden board, grasp it as close to its middle as possible so that it does not tilt. After lifting a board, raise it with extra clearance before carrying it, so that it does not hit the tower. Before every command that moves the arms, think carefully about whether this move could make an object held in a gripper hit the tower, and whether the transfer needs an intermediate waypoint to avoid it; rather spend steps on avoiding a collision than ignore the risk of one. When picking up one of the four white block pillars (the instruction's wooden blocks), if a collision seems possible, tilt the gripper before sending move_ee and then start the carry. After completing level 1 and level 2, first check whether the pillars' and boards' pose-deviation requirements are met before attempting level 3. When going from above the tower to grasp an object lower down, always move horizontally first and only then descend to grasp, so that the arm does not hit the parts of the tower already built. When picking up the green piece, do not grasp it on its slanted faces, where it slips; grasp it on flat faces. While stacking the tower, make sure the centres of the two boards are aligned.
hints.classify_objects: When placing an object into a basket, once you have confirmed it is above the basket, release it directly; there is no need to lower it first. When grasping a ring-shaped object such as a watch, prefer narrowing the gripper and grasping the ring from the inside; it is less likely to drop.
hints.fasten_screws: Each loose piece is a hexagonal nut about 35 mm across its flat sides and 19 mm thick. Before going down to pick one up, set the gripper to a pad gap of about 42 mm (`width 42`), line the opening axis up across two opposite flat sides, then close. After placing each nut on its post, press it down with a short, slow downward push of the gripper so that it sits tight. You have plenty of steps: do not end the task after only placing the screws. You must avoid any collision between the nut you carry and the posts or the other nuts: while carrying a nut, keep the fingertips at least 5 cm higher than the top of every other post and nut.
hints.imitate_sorting_sequence: When placing an object into the basket, once you have confirmed it is above the basket, release it directly; there is no need to lower it first.
hints.make_toast: Before going down to a slice, set the gripper to a pad gap of about 19 mm (`width 19`): the slices are about 1.2 cm thick and stand about 2.5 cm apart (centre to centre), leaving gaps of about 1.3 cm, and a fingertip is about 6 mm thick. Centre the TCP on the slice with the opening axis perpendicular to its faces, lower the fingers into the gaps on both sides of it, then close. If a slice has to be passed from one arm to the other, the arm holding it should turn it so that the slice itself lies horizontal (flat, not standing on an edge); the handover is easier that way. A slice lying flat on the table cannot be picked up with one gripper: it is too thin for the fingertips to get under it, and it slips. If a slice falls, do not retry one-handed grasps. First push it with a closed gripper to a place both arms can reach. Then press one gripper down on the slice to hold it still, and with the other gripper pinch it at an edge that sticks out. When taking a slice out of the rack and when putting it down or into the toaster, leave enough height: a slice is about 11.7 cm long and hangs below the fingers by nearly that much, so before moving sideways raise it until its lower edge is clear of the rack, the toaster and everything else below it (the fingertips about 12 cm or more above their tops), to avoid hitting other objects. Each slice must go all the way down into its toaster slot; a slice that rests only partly inside, sticking up or caught on the rim, does not count.
hints.stack_bowls: After picking up a bowl, lift it until it is more than 5 cm above the height of the target bowl before trying to place it on top. Stack the bowls neatly: the centres of all three bowls must be closely aligned, otherwise the stack does not count as a success.
hints.pack_objects_into_box: The box's two short ends (left and right) carry open flaps that stand up to about 18 cm above the table and lean outward; its two long sides (the one facing the robot and the far one) have no flap, and their top edge is only about 10 cm above the table. The box is very light and any collision easily moves it. Every time you put something into the box or take an arm out of it, think carefully about whether a collision could happen and whether you need an intermediate waypoint to get around obstacles; rather spend extra steps avoiding a collision than ignore the risk of one. When putting something into the box, you must come in over a side that has no flap, never over the flaps. When putting an object in, take the object's own length into account (it hangs below the fingers): the gripper fingertips must be at least 23 cm (18 + 5 cm) above the table. If needed, you may move the box to a more suitable place.
hints.play_Xylophone: Strike each bar in its middle, not at its ends. After each strike, lift the mallet straight up by at least 6 cm from the lowest point of that strike before moving to the next bar; a smaller lift will not count the next bar.
hints.play_stacking_toy: After each placement, first lift the gripper up, and make sure the current piece has slid down onto its peg before going to grasp the next piece. Time is very tight: give priority to the pegs that take fewer pieces and get their pieces correctly onto the peg first, and only then consider the other pieces.
hints.play_tic_tac_toe: Use both grippers: as long as pieces remain, whenever one arm is placing a piece, use the other arm to pick up one of the remaining pieces, so as to save the steps of doing it separately.
hints.pour_liquid_into_cup: Try to grasp the bottle near its bottom rather than at the top of its neck; that makes it easier to pour. Do not try to move the cup.
hints.push_T: Move the T by grasping it and sliding it along the table: holding it is fine as long as you do not lift it. Do not rely on pushing alone; pushing alone cannot control its position precisely.
hints.pour_balls_into_vase: Grasp the cup near its bottom rather than at its rim; that makes it easier to pour the balls out. Do not try to move the vase; its position is completely fixed.
hints.fill_egg_holder: The basket's rim is about 11 cm above the table (the basket is shallow in the middle and its wall rises toward the rim), and an egg is about 6 cm tall. After grasping an egg, lift it straight up until the bottom of the egg is at least 14 cm above the table (with a top-down grasp around the egg's middle, the TCP at about 18 cm or higher) before moving sideways, so the egg does not hit the basket. Use only one arm to pick up and place the eggs; the other arm only needs to get ready to close the lid.
hints.swap_T: Each T must end within 3° of the OTHER T's start heading, not its own; the two Ts usually start a few degrees apart, so a placement that only looks right often fails. Judge headings with the measure option `pose`, never by eye: before moving anything, measure both Ts with `pose` (top camera, a pixel on each T's top face, z = the top face's height) and note each one's xy and tail_deg; these are the targets. A straight-down grasp across the stem squares the T in the gripper: with down<ψ> its tail_deg becomes ψ + 90° or ψ - 90° (whichever is nearer its heading before the grasp), whatever it was before, and turning the wrist by Δ turns the T by Δ. So release each T with the wrist turned so that its tail_deg equals the other T's measured start tail_deg, and make that turn during the carry. After both releases, with the arms out of the top view, measure both Ts with `pose` again; if one is more than 2° or 1 cm off its target and the steps allow, grasp it again and release it corrected.
hints.sweep_blocks: The way of sweeping is not checked: prefer to pick each object up with a gripper and put it straight into the dustpan, and do not use the broom, unless an object is out of reach; then you may sweep that object into the dustpan with the broom.
hints.match_and_pick_from_conveyor: While the conveyor is running, hold for at most 50 steps at a time; a longer hold can miss what passes on the belt.
hints.swap_blocks: Lift each block at least 5 cm.
